y-m-12-05.title: If 2 lines no meet, dem parallel?
y-m-12-05.topic: Two parallel lines (distance between parallel lines)
y-m-12-05.goal: Understand say not meeting inside paper no enough to confirm parallel. Revise your judgment while considering error in distance measurements.
y-m-12-05.material: Line 가 and line 나 dey drawn for paper. You wan find out whether dem parallel. Distance between parallel lines na length measured at right angle to line 가, and e same wherever you measure am. Assume ruler measurement fit get error about 0.2 cm. y-m-12-05.thinking.2: Choose ways to make evidence stronger

y-m-12-05.s.s1.prompt: Dem go reveal data one piece at a time. Each time, choose wetin you think.

y-m-12-05.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You use fact say difference of 0.1 cm smaller than error (about 0.2 cm).
y-m-12-05.s.s1.st.1.o.b: 4.1 come out, so I conclude dem no parallel.
y-m-12-05.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Difference of 0.1 cm dey inside error range. With difference dis small, e hard to conclude dem no parallel.
y-m-12-05.s.s1.st.1.o.c: I only measure 3 places, so I no go decide whether dem parallel until I measure more.
y-m-12-05.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You point out say data small. Planning to gather more before deciding also good judgment.
y-m-12-05.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Di distances similar, so di 2 lines na same line.

y-m-12-05.s.s1.st.2.after: Difference bigger than error and keep growing in one direction, so e suitable to think say dem no parallel. If you worry about chance of error, measuring again to check also good. If you go toward side where distance smaller, dem go meet someday.

y-m-12-05.s.s1.reflect: At first you start with “no fit decide”; with second data, “chance say dem parallel” increase; with third data, your judgment change other way to “not parallel.” Notice say even though you collect data the same way, your judgment change depending on whether difference bigger or smaller than error.
y-m-12-05.s.s2.prompt: How many of these methods make evidence say line 가 and 나 parallel stronger? Choose all wey fit.

y-m-12-05.s.s2.r.c: You use fact say 2 lines perpendicular to one line must be parallel.

y-m-12-05.s.s2.r.d: Thickness no get anything to do with being parallel.
y-m-12-05.s.s2.explain: Measuring more places and checking say both perpendicular to one line make evidence for parallel stronger. Eye feeling or thickness only weakly connect with parallel.
y-m-12-05.s.s2.acc.0: Measuring more places alone make evidence stronger. Checking perpendicular too even better.
y-m-12-05.s.s2.acc.1: Checking perpendicular alone na evidence for parallel. Adding measurement even better.

y-m-12-01.topic: Measuring angle size with protractor (reading two rows of marks)
y-m-12-01.goal: Find standard to decide which number to read from two rows of marks on protractor, and correct wrong reading by checking against estimated size.

If you read row wey start from right 0°, na 65; if from left 0°, na 115. Dis angle look narrower than right angle (right-angle corner of set square). Picture no dey, so imagine position wey words describe.

y-m-12-01.s.s2.r.b: You estimate by comparing with right angle and choose value wey fit estimate. Remember too say for previous question smaller value correct with same method.
y-m-12-01.s.s2.o.c: 75°: Smaller of both values always more accurate
y-m-12-01.s.s2.r.c: You choose based on number size. Estimate whether angle wider or narrower than right angle.
y-m-12-01.s.s2.o.d: No fit decide: because dem write both numbers on protractor
y-m-12-01.s.s2.r.d: Even if dem write both numbers, you fit choose one if you use standard (di aligned 0°, estimate).
y-m-12-01.s.s2.explain: Dis time, 105 for row wey start from right 0° correct. For previous question, smaller number correct, and this time bigger number correct. So standard no be number size but 'row wey start from aligned 0°' and 'whether angle wider or narrower than right angle'.

y-m-12-04.title: Grounds for saying “all quadrilaterals”

y-m-12-04.s.s2.r.a: You understand am as common measurement error. E also show say error small and spread on both sides of 360°.

y-m-12-04.s.s2.r.b: 358° and 362° miss by similar amount on both sides. Check whether dem keep missing only one side.

y-m-12-14.title: When temperature for 2 villages become equal?
y-m-12-14.topic: Where 2 line graphs cross (meaning of hidden times between measurements)
y-m-12-14.goal: Separate values for measured times from values wey you guess by joining points between dem, then revise your guess when new measurement come.
y-m-12-14.material: On same day, dem measure temperature for Village 가 and Village 나 only 2 times, 10 a.m. and 12 noon (unit: °C). Village 가 na 20°C at 10 and 24°C at 12. Village 나 na 24°C at 10 and 22°C at 12. When dem join points for each village with line segments on same graph, di 2 lines cross between 10 and 12. y-m-12-14.thinking.0: Separate wetin data prove from wetin need assumption
y-m-12-14.thinking.1: Assess claim wey talk guess like say na certain
y-m-12-14.s.s1.prompt: Choose all wetin you fit say you know from dis data.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.hint.0: First compare which village temperature higher at 10 and at 12.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.hint.1: Sort each statement into: read directly from measured values, need assumption, or no evidence.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.a: At 10, Village 나 temperature 4°C higher than Village 가.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.a: Na difference between measured values 24 and 20. You fit read am from direct measurements.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.b: At 11, temperature for both villages probably same (if you join 2 points with line segment).
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.b: Dem no measure at 11. Even if you guess by joining segments, temperature no equal at 11.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.c: At 12, Village 가 temperature 2°C higher than Village 나.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.c: Na difference between measured values 24 and 22. You fit read am from direct measurements.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.d: There probably one time between 10 and 12 when temperature for both villages same.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.d: You say am using both fact say which one higher switch and assumption say “temperature change continuously.”
y-m-12-14.s.s1.o.e: Between 10 and 12, temperature difference between villages stay 4°C.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.r.e: At 10 difference na 4°C, but at 12 Village 가 become warmer, so difference change.
y-m-12-14.s.s1.explain: a and c na measured values. d say Village 나 warmer at 10 and Village 가 warmer at 12, so if temperature change continuously, dem must be one time between when dem become equal. b na value at 11 wey no measure, so no evidence; e no match value at 12.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.prompt: Yuri talk, “If you calculate where di 2 line segments meet, na around 11:20, and temperature then about 22.7°C.” How we suppose understand dis statement?
y-m-12-14.s.s2.hint.0: Check whether anybody directly measure temperature at 11:20.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.hint.1: Think whether temperature fit go up and down between 2 points.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.o.a: You fit call am settled fact, same as value measured at 11:20.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.r.a: Nobody measure at 11:20. Na value dem calculate by joining 2 points.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.o.b: Dat wrong. Temperature of both villages no fit become same between 10 and 12.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.r.b: Di order at 10 and 12 don switch, so if temperatures change continuously, there must be time when dem equal.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.o.c: Na only guess based on assumption say temperature change steadily between 2 points.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.r.c: You separate guess from measured values and point out assumption say “e change steadily.”
y-m-12-14.s.s2.o.d: Calculation correct, so if we measure at 11:20 e go definitely be 22.7°C.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.r.d: No guarantee di change between points steady. If dem measure for real, result fit different.
y-m-12-14.s.s2.explain: Value wey dem calculate by joining 2 points with straight line na guess say “e fit be so.” E match real life only if assumption say temperature change at steady rate correct.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.prompt: I measure again at 11, and Village 가 na 21°C, Village 나 na 23.5°C. After learning dis new value, how you go revise your thinking about when both village temperatures become equal? Use new value as evidence.

y-m-12-14.s.s3.hint.1: Combine am with which village warmer at 12, and think around when dem become equal.
y-m-12-14.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You use new values (21°C, 23.5°C) as evidence?
y-m-12-14.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You compare which village warmer at 11?

y-m-12-14.s.s3.model.0: For 11 o'clock, Village 가 get 21°C and Village 나 get 23.5°C, so Village 나 still dey hotter. For 12 o'clock, Village 가 dey hotter, so di time dem become equal shift to between 11 and 12. 11:20 no correct.

y-m-12-14.s.s3.modelNote.1: E still talk say dem need measure more.

y-m-12-08.title: Same data: which graph fit?

y-m-12-08.thinking.1: Comparing reasons when several answers possible
y-m-12-08.thinking.2: Distinguishing wetin data fit tell and wetin you need find out more
y-m-12-08.prereq.0: How to read bar and line graphs

y-m-12-08.s.s3.prompt: Looking at graph, book number especially small for July (20 books) and August (12 books). One padi talk, 'E low because na vacation.' Graph or table alone fit tell reason? Write separately wetin you fit know for sure from graph and wetin you need find out more about.

y-m-12-08.s.s3.hint.1: To check whether vacation claim correct, think one date or question wey you need.

y-m-12-09.title: A table where “Other” na di biggest category
y-m-12-09.topic: Choose categories to sort data (“Other” category)
y-m-12-09.goal: Find problem with table where “Other” cell biggest, then make several better ways to arrange di same data by splitting categories.
y-m-12-09.material: 24 Grade 4 students each answer which activity dem want do pass during break. Everybody choose only one. y-m-12-09.thinking.1: Make several ways to arrange with conditions
y-m-12-09.prereq.0: Count data by category and arrange am in table
y-m-12-09.prereq.1: Table total must equal number of people wey answer survey
y-m-12-09.s.s1.prompt: How we suppose understand “Other na di most” for dis table?

y-m-12-09.s.s1.hint.1: Think wetin person wey dey look di table go most wan know.
y-m-12-09.s.s1.o.a: You fit tell say Other activity popular pass, so Jiyun arrange di table well.
y-m-12-09.s.s1.r.a: “Other” na cell wey bundle different activities. E no be one popular activity.

y-m-12-09.s.s1.r.c: Correct total and useful table na different things.
y-m-12-09.s.s1.o.d: If you remove Other cell, every student choose one of di four.
y-m-12-09.s.s1.r.d: If you remove Other, table get no place to put activities wey those 9 people choose.
y-m-12-09.s.s1.explain: If Other biggest, you no fit know wetin popular. If you split di activities wey 9 people choose into categories, table go more useful. Whether total correct na another matter.
y-m-12-09.s.s2.prompt: Split di 9 people for Other again into jump rope (g1 people), tag (g2 people), and Other (h people), then make new table. Conditions: all 3 cells get at least 1 person, and total na 9. Also Other no suppose pass any other cell (soccer 6, reading 5, drawing 4, jump rope, tag). Make 3 different tables.

y-m-12-09.s.s2.because.prompt: Write one sentence why e good make Other cell no be di biggest.

y-m-12-11.title: Can asking 10 people tell us about whole grade?
y-m-12-11.topic: How to choose who to survey (who to ask so you fit talk about whole grade?)
y-m-12-11.goal: Understand say range wey you fit claim from same result depend on whether surveyed people represent everybody, then revise judgment when new information come.
y-m-12-11.material: Minho school get 100 Grade 4 students. Minho wan know “sport wey Grade 4 students like pass.” He ask dem choose only one sport. How much you fit trust result depend on how Minho choose who to ask.
y-m-12-11.thinking.0: Notice di limits of how dem collect data
y-m-12-11.thinking.1: Revise how sure you be when new information come
y-m-12-11.prereq.0: Show survey results with tables and bar graphs
y-m-12-11.s.s1.prompt: Information go come one piece at a time. Each time, choose wetin you fit say about “all Grade 4.”
y-m-12-11.s.s1.hint.0: First sort out wetin kind people answer di survey.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.hint.1: Separate whether new information change di numbers or change how to understand di numbers.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.info: Minho ask 10 friends wey sit together with am for lunch. Result na soccer 7 people, basketball 2, running 1.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.ask: From dis result, you fit say “for all Grade 4, soccer na wetin dem like pass”?
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.after: E clear fact say 7 out of 10 choose soccer. But to talk about all Grade 4, check whether those 10 represent everybody well.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Yes. 7 out of 10, so probably soccer go also be most popular for all Grade 4, like that.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.r.a: No reason yet to expand result from 10 people to all 100. Who those 10 be matter.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Soccer come out top, but na only 10 friends wey sit together, so we no know for sure about all Grade 4 yet.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You separate result from one part from di whole group.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.o.c: No fit say. 10 small compared with 100, so e useless completely.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Result from 10 people still be information. E just no enough to talk about “everybody.”
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.info: E turn out say di 10 wey sit together for lunch all be friends from same soccer club.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.ask: After you hear dis, wetin happen to your thinking about all Grade 4?
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.after: Your first judgment na “no sure yet,” so e okay to keep am. E also okay to say di reason don clear. Main ting na say hard to talk about all Grade 4 from these 10 people.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Soccer na di most. Even if some people dey soccer club, fact remain say 7 choose am.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.r.a: E fact say 7 choose am, but reason to apply result to all Grade 4 don weaker.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Now e hard to trust as result for all Grade 4. These 10 people likely like soccer.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You notice say surveyed people fit lean one way.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.o.c: My first thinking say e no sure still remain, and di reason don clearer.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You keep your first judgment and sort out how new information make di reason stronger.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.o.d: E mean say no Grade 4 student like soccer.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.1.r.d: From these 10 people alone, conclusion “nobody like am” no follow.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.info: Minho again choose 20 students by drawing numbers, 4 from each of Grade 4 classes 1 to 5, and ask dem. Result na soccer 6, basketball 5, running 4, jump rope 3, Other 2.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.ask: Wetin you fit say from result for these 20?
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.after: Dem choose same number from each class by drawing numbers, so e represent all Grade 4 better than di first survey. Still, soccer and basketball difference small, so hard to make strong claim; asking more students go make am more certain.

y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Soccer dey small ahead, but 6 and 5 differ by small amount, so hard to claim say na wetin dem like pass.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.r.b: From data wey represent people better, you also think about how big di difference be.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Basketball na hidden number 1, because di result differ by class.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.r.c: No reason for dat. Data show soccer get 1 person more.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.o.d: You fit see soccer small pass, and asking more students go make am more certain.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You only say as much as current data let you, and also say how to make am more certain.
y-m-12-11.s.s1.reflect: First result from 10 was “no sure yet,” and when soccer club information come, reason become clear. When survey happen by another method, result change and range of wetin you fit say expand small. Notice even with same numbers, wetin you fit say depend on “who you ask.”
y-m-12-11.s.s2.prompt: Even if you survey same 20 students, which method best represent all Grade 4?
y-m-12-11.s.s2.hint.0: For each method, imagine one by one whether friends wey dem pick look like all Grade 4.
y-m-12-11.s.s2.hint.1: Compare whether method pick only friends from one class or pick people from every class.
y-m-12-11.s.s2.o.a: Ask first 20 people you meet near soccer goal for playground.
y-m-12-11.s.s2.r.a: Near soccer goal, there fit be more students wey like soccer.
y-m-12-11.s.s2.o.b: Pick same number from each class by drawing numbers.
y-m-12-11.s.s2.r.b: Every student get chance to be picked, and di bias between classes go smaller.

y-m-12-11.s.s2.r.c: If you ask di same people again, only number of answers increase; number of new people thoughts no increase.

y-m-12-12.title: Di top choice in 2 classes and di top choice for whole grade
